main_text.p: butionem,quam ipse sua concauitate præ-stat.Quod sanitatis genus ex partium simi-larium proba compositione, numero, magnitudine & figura constat, quemadmodum nos docet Galenus lib. de Sanit. tuenda 1. Postea ut morbum totius substantiæ Ferne-lius confirmet, testimonio utitur Galeni, Cap.7.qui quinto libro de Simplicium medicamentorum facultatibus profert, medicamenta alterare, aut una quapiam qualitate, nempe calefaciendo, aut refrigerando, aut humectando, aut exiccando, aut dictorum coniugatione quapiā: aut tota sua substan-tia, ficuti complura lethalium, uenenorum, nec pauca alexiteriorum seu amuletorum, & purgantia omnia, & multa, quæ uocant Cap.18.attrahentia, profert. Est & alter in eodem libro locus, quo in eandem sententiam idem Galenus scribit duplicem esse alexiteriorum naturam: aut enim commutare, aut ex affecto corpore pellere bestiarū uirus corrumpendi natura præditū, uel mortiferum medicamentum: & commutare quidem, aut una tantum qualitate, aut duabus in unum coniugatis, aut totis substantijs, inanire uero totius substantiæ similitudine, & calore cum partium tenuitate coiuncto.

page.notes: Marginal notes "Cap.7." and "Cap.18." are beside the lines of the text in the left margin; the reference at "Cap.18." was placed beside the line with "attrahentia". Some words in the body are doubtful because of the scan. The text "ut morbum totius substantiæ" and "substantiæ" were read from "fubftantiæ"; the word "tota fua" is clear. The line "Hæc" at the foot is a catchword, not a paragraph; it is also transcribed in main text, which should be checked. Several words near the right edge are cut by the scan.
